projects.name: Jacuzzi perimeter joint repair
projects.status: Planning; sanitary silicone selected and removal pending

reasons: This is the newest meaningful DIY activity, including in-store sanitary-silicone selection
The rigid failing border can admit moisture and should be replaced with a flexible joint
Manual tools avoid dependence on the delayed Milwaukee multi-tool and reduce risk to the acrylic tub

projects.labor: 3–5 h for removal, cleaning, masking, and sealing, plus manufacturer-specified cure time with the jacuzzi filled
projects.cost: Estimated ₡4.100–₡15.000 remaining, depending on whether a scraper, tape, or backer rod is needed
projects.assumption: Redo the entire joint along the two walls, not the normal tile grout lines. Aim for a continuous approximately 5–7 mm white silicone bead; use backer rod only where the cleaned cavity is too deep for a correctly shaped sealant joint.
nextTasks: Test-remove a short section using a utility knife and stiff scraper, keeping metal edges away from the acrylic.
Remove the full failing tub-to-tile border, vacuum it, remove residue, and let the joint dry completely.
Install backer rod only in deep cavities, then fill the jacuzzi to its normal operating level.
Mask both sides, apply one continuous white 100% sanitary silicone bead, tool it smooth, remove tape, and leave the tub filled through the stated cure time.

materials.item: Ceys Stop Moho white 100% sanitary silicone
materials.note: Identified in store at approximately ₡4.100; one cartridge should be enough for the two photographed sides, but purchase was not confirmed.

materials.quantity: Only for cavities approximately 8–10 mm or deeper after removal; 6 mm rod is a provisional size
materials.note: Do not buy until the old joint is removed unless it is inexpensive and convenient; shallow portions do not need it.
Mask both sides for a straight 5–7 mm finished bead.
Vacuum dust, remove residue, and dry completely before sealing.

tools: Stiff putty knife or narrow plastic-safe scraper
Manual carbide grout-removal tool for hard material

sources.label: EPA Costa Rica bathroom silicone reference

projects.name: Rusted metal door-frame base repair

reasons: Active corrosion should be stopped before section loss advances
The damage appears concentrated in the lowest approximately 2–4 cm and may remain repairable without frame replacement
The work can proceed with hand tools and the available orbital sander

projects.labor: 4–8 h across preparation, treatment, priming, painting, and sealing, plus product drying and cure times
projects.cost: Estimated ₡22.000–₡45.000 remaining if the exposed metal is solid; perforation repair or section replacement is not included
projects.assumption: The visible corrosion appears localized near the floor, but all loose scale must be removed before deciding whether coating is enough. Identify and correct trapped-water entry at the metal-to-porcelain joint so the corrosion does not recur.
nextTasks: Scrape loose paint and rust from the full affected base, then sand with approximately 60–80 and 120 grit.
Probe the cleaned metal; stop and reassess if it is perforated, paper-thin, or crumbles under pressure.
If solid, treat residual rust, apply compatible anticorrosive primer, and repaint the entire lower black rail for a uniform finish.
After the coating cures, seal the metal-to-porcelain joint with a flexible exterior sealant and confirm the water source is corrected.

materials.note: EPA listed SUR Corrostop 1 L at ₡6.950 on 2026-09-10.
EPA listed black matte Corrostyl 1/4 gal at ₡7.250 on 2026-09-10; confirm compatibility with the topcoat system.
Paint the full lower rail rather than isolated patches.
Use at the cured metal-to-porcelain joint; do not use grout or cement.

materials.quantity: 2–4 sheets each in 60–80 and approximately 120 grit
materials.note: Use hand sanding in corners and the orbital only on accessible flat areas.

tools: Gloves, eye protection, and suitable dust protection

projects.name: Drywall movement-joint repair

reasons: The long recurring inside-corner crack indicates movement rather than a simple paint defect
A fastening check determines whether the repair should be flexible or retaped
The repair can prevent repeated cosmetic failures without relying on delayed tools

projects.labor: 4–10 h over multiple visits for inspection, preparation, compound or sealant, sanding, priming, and painting, plus drying time
projects.cost: Estimated ₡12.000–₡35.000 remaining, depending on whether the drywall moves and must be refastened and retaped
projects.assumption: If the drywall is solid, use a small consistent joint with high-quality paintable elastomeric or acrylic sealant to tolerate approximately 1–2 mm movement. If it moves, correct fastening first and retape the inside corner with paper tape and setting-type compound.
nextTasks: Press along the cracked ceiling or soffit transition and mark any drywall movement.
Remove loose compound and failed tape only along the affected corner.
If movement exists, add or reseat screws into confirmed framing and retape with paper tape plus setting-type compound; if solid, form a small flexible paintable joint.
Feather as needed, sand, prime, and repaint only after the repair system has dried or cured.

materials.quantity: 1 × approximately 300 ml cartridge if the board is solid
materials.note: EPA listed paintable acrylic and urethane-acrylic options around ₡3.895–₡4.395 on 2026-09-10.
Use paper, not mesh, for an inside-corner retape.

materials.quantity: 1 small bag if refastening and retaping are required
materials.note: Use for the initial taped repair, then feather with finishing compound.
Install only into confirmed framing.
Measure after deciding the repair method.

tools: Caulking gun if using flexible joint
